title: A float key beyond the range of a double and .inf are different keys
notes: `1e400` is the finite value 10^400 and `.inf` is not a finite number, so the two keys are different and the mapping has no duplicate: section 3.2.1.3 calls scalars equal only when their tags and canonical forms are equal, and the canonical forms of the two differ (section 10.2.1.4 gives `.inf` its own form). Section 10.2.1.4 also says a float is an approximation whose range depends on the implementation, so it does not say how a library that cannot hold 10^400 must read the key. The kit compares float keys outside the range of a double by their exact decimal value (docs/edit-semantics.md, Refusals: 'Two float keys whose values lie outside the finite non-zero range of a binary64 double'), which makes this a convention and the case carries the tag. The answer is exact, so the edit below finds `.inf` by its text (RFC 6901 section 4) and changes only its value, or the library refuses the document with a `limit` error, as it may for integers beyond 64 bits. It must not report `duplicate-key`. The case is a patch because the kit has no value for a float beyond the range of a double (a document would be read as infinity). The edit must change `b` only.

provenance.reference: A key identity that rounded 1e400 to infinity, so it equalled the key .inf and a valid mapping was refused as a duplicate.
